I don’t know if the rate cuts were “profoundly mistaken” last year. It depends on what fiscal policies and macro outlook were assumed. I never thought we were returning to the old/pre-COVID world. A structurally more inflationary regime was inevitable. 

The international comparison isn’t really very meaningful. Europe is structurally weak along several key dimensions. That’s why inflation quickly went back down and likely will remain low. The structurally low growth economies would’ve all had low inflation if they had reasonably large supply elasticities. The UK would’ve too if they didn’t exit from the EU. Japan is externally dependent on energy and has low supply elasticity hence all their current struggles with inflation despite weak growth fundamentals.

tweets.text:
I hated the last memecoin run and said so loudly.

this one feels different though.

for the first time in a very long time it feels like we’re actually onboarding net new people. and it’s not because the coins got any better or the shitcoiners got any less extractive, but because this time there’s a much bigger social aspect to it, and it feels a lot more like we’re experimenting with genuinely new things that interesting stuff can grow out of down the line.

I still think memecoins are dumb and I’m not participating. I also don’t get why we’re going this crazy about a new chain like Robinhood in an era where this should be abstracted away and shouldn’t matter at all.

but I like the novel, social experiments, and the second and third order effects they can bring to make the pie grow again.

$SYH.V $SYHBF #uranium
Most uranium juniors need one drill program to work.

Skyharbour is entering the final stretch of 2026 with more than 30,000 metres planned across six Athabasca projects, while partners fund much of the exploration and send cash and shares back to $SYH.

Meanwhile, the prospect-generator machine keeps expanding:

⚒️ 44 Athabasca projects
⚒️ 11 partner companies
⚒️ Up to C$131M in potential exploration spending, cash and shares
⚒️ Assays expected through year-end and into 2027

Few juniors offer this combination of wholly owned high-grade discovery upside, a major strategic partner in Denison and multiple partner-funded shots on goal.
Skyharbour does not need everything to work. One meaningful discovery could change the valuation completely.

Imagine a country losing $2T a year with $32T of debt.

That's the U.S. and Ray Dalio just broke down how it ends.

Yields spiked, Bitcoin dumped, and macro matters again.

Here are the top 8 reads this week:

Ray Dalio On What's Happening To The US

He analyzes the country like a business: $5.5T coming in, $7.5T going out, $32T of debt, and about $1T of interest eating 20% of revenue.

He also tells investors exactly where to sit. Bonds, gold, Bitcoin, with percentages.

The Failure Of Bitcoin Maximalism

Nic came with receipts. Stock-to-flow failed. Alts didn't go to zero, they're worth $600B excluding stablecoins. No country holds Bitcoin as legal tender. Lightning moves maybe $10B a year against stablecoins' $15T.

BTC as an asset has won, but the ideology has failed.

SOL Thesis

TLDR: SOL is one of three index assets alongside BTC and ETH that get reflexively bid once it's clear we're back. It spent the last 10 months being sold by everyone who wasn't committed.

Stablecoin volume now rivals Ethereum, Tron and Base. Tokenized equity volume leads all L1s.

Zcash Thesis

Grayscale's case: ZEC sits at roughly $8B, which is 0.6% of the Currencies crypto sector. At 5% of that segment it's about 9x from here.

Privacy feels inevitable to me. The market disagrees. That's the whole trade.

A Balanced Take On RAIL

21.2% yield, about half of it funded by reserves and dilution rather than fees. Supply went from 57.5M to 60M.

There's a live vote to deploy RAILGUN to Base. But a new chain alone doesn't fix the bottleneck. You need distribution. No mainstream wallet exposes RAILGUN to users yet. Kohaku is the catalyst to watch.

SEC's New Proposal, Explained By Lawyers

MetaLeX pulled the parts that matter out of a 402-page document for us plebs. My read: it's good, or at least as good as anything realistically on the table.

Caveats: it doesn't cover market infrastructure, and it isn't live law yet.

The Packaging Problem

TradFi's real problem isn't fees. It's that every asset gets unpacked, verified, reconciled and repacked each time it crosses from one institution to another.

Aleks argues tokens remove that friction the way shipping containers did for freight.

A Trillion Times Larger

"Most of the money to be made comes from investors best equipped to un-entangle those two variables before everyone else does."

The two variables: how good the business actually is, and how far away its future cash flows sit. Every multiple blends them and tells you neither. Separating them before consensus does is the edge.

When you go off the main path and do something else, then apply it back to the main path… the path gets more extraordinary.

I started @draper_u just to help entrepreneurs get started.

Now it's a major pre-accelerator, a great source of deal flow, a powerful network connector for my venture business.

Elon does this at scale:

→ SpaceX + Tesla + Battery factory + Starlink all helping each other

→ Connecting Starlink to cars

→ Twitter (X) + XAI using Twitter's data for better AI

→ That AI is improving space, cars, batteries

Synergies take time. You need a long vision.

But when you go deep into one category, then another, you can start thinking about how they mesh.
